### C-R4-01
**Claim:** Tsumura treats 2 Sam 10–12 as set against the Ammon war background: for empire it leads to domination of Syrian kingdoms (10:15-19; 8:3-12), but more importantly for the biblical writer it is the setting for David’s great sin; literarily the Ammonite war is a “frame” for David and Bathsheba in 11:1–12:25. These chapters may chronologically precede 8:2-3.
**Quote:** “the story of the Ammonite war constitutes a ‘frame’ for the story of David and Bathsheba in 11:1-12:25.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 1–10; §H intro (10:1–12:31)
**Targets:** [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]], [[david]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R4-02
**Claim:** Like ch. 9, ch. 10 begins with David’s ḥesed concern—here toward Hanun son of Nahash (presumably 1 Sam 11’s Nahash, later ally vs Saul). Ammonite leaders reject the consolers as spies; Hanun humiliates the envoys (half beard; garments cut to buttocks = symbolic demasculization; cf. Isa 20:4), breaking relations and declaring war. David lets them stay at Jericho until beards grow (direct road Rabbah–Jerusalem).
**Quote:** “Humiliation by shaving off half of the beard and by cutting off the garment in half up to the buttocks … was probably symbolic demasculization.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 12–56; 10:1-5
**Targets:** [[2-samuel]], [[david]], [[david-tsumura]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R4-03
**Claim:** Against Rost/Flanagan/Gunn (Aramean war secondary), Tsumura follows McCarter/Hertzberg: ch. 10 is a unit—Zobah coalition intervention fits both parties given Israelite threat; geography and later Ammonite epigraphy support Aramean help. Ammon hires Beth-rehob, Zobah (20,000 foot), Maacah (1,000), Tob (12,000); Joab and the army go; Ammon at gate of Rabbah, Arameans in the field. nibʾăšû “become odious” = hated by; Olyan as technical covenant violation—Tsumura notes 1 Sam 13:4 is not covenant violation.
**Quote:** “McCarter, following Hertzberg, takes chapter 10 as a unit, since the intervention of the Zobah coalition would be consistent with the interests of both parties.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 58–87; 10:6-8
**Targets:** [[2-samuel]], [[joab]], [[david-tsumura]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R4-04
**Claim:** Joab, trapped before and behind, assigns select men to Aram and rest to Abishai vs Ammon; speech: help each other; “Be strong… for our people and the cities of our God”; “the LORD… will do what is good in his eyes.” Arameans flee; Ammonites retreat into the city; Joab returns to Jerusalem (Abishai presumably maintains siege). “cities of our God” (ʿārê ʾĕlōhênû) kept as MT; Giveon/Kuntillet Ajrud (“Yahweh of Samaria/Teman”) may support Yahweh’s cities in Transjordan, or simply Israelite cities.
**Quote:** “Be strong and behave courageously on behalf of our people and the cities of our God! As for the LORD, he will do what is good in his eyes.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 90–122; 10:9-14
**Targets:** [[joab]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R4-05
**Claim:** Hadadezer brings Arameans from beyond the Euphrates to Helam under Shobach; David crosses Jordan, defeats them (700 charioteers; 40,000 horsemen; Shobach dies). Hadadezer’s vassals make peace and serve Israel—exchange of suzerainty (not necessarily “treaty/covenant status” per McCarthy); Malamat: David took over Hadadezer’s realm territorially and structurally. Arameans fear to help Ammon again. Not necessarily a separate secondary campaign.
**Quote:** “They thus exchanged Israelite for Aramean suzerainty. The expression itself does not necessarily denote ‘treaty or covenant status.’”
**Locus:** slice ll. 124–160; 10:15-19
**Targets:** [[2-samuel]], [[david]], [[david-tsumura]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R4-06
**Claim:** **AXB embedding (priority):** Chs. 11–12 (David and Bathsheba) are embedded in the Ammonite war between 11:1 and 12:26-31 as a **frame**: “Joab – Rabbah” and “David – Jerusalem” in 11:1 correspond to 12:26-31 (begins Joab–Rabbah, ends David–Jerusalem). 11:1b (“Now David was staying at Jerusalem”) is SETTING for EVENT v. 2; vv. 1–2 integral regardless of Joab/David contrast emphasis. Parallel 1 Chr 20:1-3 is AB without X interruption.
**Quote:** “It is embedded in the story of the Ammonite war of David, that is, between 11:1 and 12:26-31, which constitute a ‘frame’… thus constituting the AXB pattern.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 162–165, 890–893; intro 11:1–12:25; 12:26-31 close

### C-R4-07
**Claim:** **“Great turning point” (priority):** The story of David and Bathsheba is “the ‘great turning point’ of the entire story of David.” Alter: writer “pulled out all the stops… crucially pivotal episode.” Why a negative story amid victory? Narrator warns: even the most successful king may do evil in the eyes of the LORD (v. 27); military/political success blinds David spiritually before the holy sovereign God.
**Quote:** “The story of ‘David and Bathsheba’ is the ‘great turning point’ of the entire story of David.”

### C-R4-08
**Claim:** **Sin escalation covet→adultery→murder (priority):** Once David broke the tenth commandment in his heart, outward actions escalate to adultery then murder:
- X: “You shall not covet” (Exod 20:17)
- VII: “You shall not commit adultery” (v. 14)
- VI: “You shall not murder” (v. 13)
Only God’s grace makes David realize his sin and accept him again as sinner by the holy Lord. Restated at 12:1 intro: broke tenth, then seventh, then sixth while the Lord silently watched.
**Quote:** “Once he broke the tenth commandment in his heart, his outward actions escalate even to breaking the commandment against murder.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 168–176, 500; intro; 12:1 frame
**Targets:** [[david]], [[david-tsumura]], [[bathsheba]], [[2-samuel]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R4-09
**Claim:** Bar-Efrat narrative-speed structure of 11:2-27: Quick Bathsheba (2-5) / Slow Uriah (6-15) / Quick Uriah death (16-17) / Slow Uriah report (18-25) / Quick Bathsheba (26-27). David’s misconduct presented bluntly without explanation so motivation does not mitigate the crime. McCarter’s “king who takes” (1 Sam 8) prophetic-history link: Tsumura distinguishes—1 Sam describes normal monarchical costs; taking an officer’s wife was not a king’s right.
**Quote:** “David’s misconduct is presented bluntly and without explanation, as if any hint of his motivation might mitigate his crime.”

### C-R4-10
**Claim:** **MT/discourse — tešûbat haššānāh / messengers vs kings (11:1a):** Tsumura rejects spring-campaign “kings go out” as forced. MT K. hmlʾkym unambiguously “messengers”; some MSS/LXX/Chr “kings.” Gordon: aleph may salvage David as war-lord; Bodner: intentional ambiguity. Tsumura: simplest is MT with aleph = messengers; malʾāk is Leitwort of ch. 11 (vv. 1, 4, 19, 22, 23, 25). Phonetic path can make mlkym ambiguous; hmlʾkym is not. “Turn of the year” ~ Ugaritic nqpt ʿd — start of administrative year when ruler sends messengers, not necessarily spring season. Even if “kings,” hard to read as critique of David staying in Jerusalem (civic duties; he follows field events). With Arameans defeated, free to besiege Rabbah (~22 mi E of Jordan; ~1000 m down + up).
**Quote:** “The term messenger (malʾāk) certainly functions as a Leitwort in this chapter… We would like to take the simplest solution, taking the MT consonantal form, with aleph, as ‘messengers.’”
**Locus:** slice ll. 196–227; 11:1a
**Targets:** [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]], [[joab]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R4-11
**Claim:** 11:1b–5: David yôšēb at ease in Jerusalem vs Joab at war; sees beautiful woman bathing (likely menstrual purification Lev 15:19-24—so child not Uriah’s); inquires—Bathsheba daughter of Eliam, wife of Uriah the Hittite; sends messengers, takes her, lies with her (she had been purified), she returns, conceives, reports “I am pregnant.” Parallel Gen 3:6 Eve “took”; temptation when relaxed. “Took” (*lqḥ) is adultery initiated by covetousness, not identical to 1 Sam 8 royal rights. “she came to him” may imply consent. Circumstantial clause (purified) subordinate to prior “lay” (MT atnah; resultative participle)—at intercourse she had purified from menstrual uncleanness; thus she knew the child was David’s. Cover-up attempt in 6–13 makes open intention at summons unlikely—ostensible welfare inquiry / private interview.
**Quote:** “His ‘taking’ was the sin of adultery, initiated by covetousness in his heart… she ‘had been purified from her uncleanness’… Accordingly she knew the child she conceived was David’s.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 228–273; 11:1b-5
**Targets:** [[david]], [[bathsheba]], [[david-tsumura]], [[2-samuel]]
*(Uriah: Misc flag — “the Hittite,” listed among “thirty” 23:39; name “Yah is my light”; Neo-Hittite/Aramean family background; Muraoka: fivefold “Hittite” may hint different treatment if Israelite—does not excuse; Firth Saul-threat guess “farfetched”)*

### C-R4-13
**Claim:** David–Uriah cover-up (11:6-15): instead of repenting openly, David tries to make Bathsheba’s child appear Uriah’s. Three escalations of David’s speech to Uriah (vv. 8, 10, 12); moral contrast sharpens. “Wash your feet” = refresh, possibly sexual euphemism. Uriah sleeps at palace door—ritual purity (Exod 19:15; Lev 15:18; 1 Sam 21:5; Deut 23:9) still on duty vs David. Uriah’s speech: ark, Israel, Judah in booths; Joab/servants on battlefield—shall I eat/drink/lie with wife? By your life… never. Contrast 2 Sam 7:1-2 (David uneasy while ark in curtains); Uriah almost reflects Ps 132:3-5—ironic. “Booths” not likely Succoth base (too far from Rabbah; Joab already at city). David makes him drunk; still does not go home. Letter by Uriah’s hand: put him at front of severe fighting and withdraw so he dies. sēper for “letter” may mark antiquity (LBH ʾiggeret). Sealed letter; both David and Joab likely literate (too dangerous via scribes). Alter: loyal Uriah won’t open letter; if he knows adultery, grim resignation.
**Quote:** “David said to Uriah three times (vv. 8, 10, 12), thus escalating his attempt to cover up his transgression… ‘Put Uriah in the front line of the severe fighting and withdraw from him, and he will be struck and be dead.’”
**Locus:** slice ll. 274–379; 11:6-15
**Targets:** [[david]], [[joab]], [[bathsheba]], [[david-tsumura]], [[2-samuel]]
*(Uriah: Misc flag — foil of fidelity; ark-loyalty; letter-bearer of own death order)*

### C-R4-17
**Claim:** **Nathan sent as counter-messenger (priority):** As David sent messengers to Bathsheba (v. 4), Joab (v. 6), Bathsheba again (v. 27) to commit adultery, camouflage, murder, marry—so the Lord sends Nathan to confront the same prophet who gave the eternal house promise in ch. 7. Accuses David of standing above God’s law; unlike deified Canaanite kings, Israel’s king under the law (1 Sam 12:25). Mari prophets sent about temple repair, not repairing people/king–god relationship. Legal trap pattern: 2 Sam 14:5-17; 1 K 20:39-43—king judges and condemns himself. Nathan = personal counselor (cf. 7:3).
**Quote:** “so here the Lord sends his messenger Nathan to David to confront him and condemn his great sin—the same prophet Nathan who had given David the promise of an eternal house in ch. 7.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 498–502; 12:1-15a intro
**Targets:** [[nathan]], [[david]], [[davidic-covenant]], [[bathsheba]], [[david-tsumura]], [[2-samuel]]

### C-R4-18
**Claim:** **Nathan’s parable (12:1-6):** Two men, rich (many sheep/cattle) vs poor (one little ewe-lamb bought, raised with children, ate/drank/lay in bosom—like daughter; three impf. habit verbs same order as Uriah 11:11). Visitor; rich reluctant to take own; took poor man’s lamb. David angry: as LORD lives, man deserves to die (ben-māwet); repay ewe fourfold (Ex 22:1; McCarter “sevenfold” LXX). *lqḥ of lamb = David took Bathsheba; heinous because he had plenty. King should protect poor (Exod 23:6 etc.; Ps 72; Krt epic). Alter: trap snaps shut—David condemns himself. Fourfold sets up later bereavement of four sons (v. 6 ↔ death of child + Amnon, Absalom, Adonijah).
**Quote:** “Nathan’s rhetorical trap has now snapped shut. David, by his access of anger, condemns himself… ‘You are the man!’”
**Locus:** slice ll. 504–564, 690; 12:1-6 (and link at 14)
**Targets:** [[nathan]], [[david]], [[bathsheba]], [[david-tsumura]], [[2-samuel]]

### C-R4-19
**Claim:** **“You are the man!” + oracle (12:7-12) (priority):** ʾattāh hāʾîš S-P marked: “the person you condemned… is none other than you” (Muraoka). Thus says the LORD God of Israel: I anointed you, delivered from Saul, gave master’s house/women, Israel and Judah; if little, would add. Why despised word of LORD doing evil? Uriah struck with sword; wife taken; killed with sword of Ammonites—**AXB tricolon** (A murder / X taking wife / B Ammonite sword ballast); Janzen via Tsumura: focus not so much murder/adultery (adultery not even explicit) as **taking Bathsheba**—usurping God’s role; hence confession “against the LORD” only (v. 13; Ps 51:4). “Despised word” may euphemize “despised the LORD” (LXXL/Theod.).
**Quote:** “You are the man!… what God focuses on in this oracle as a whole is… ‘David’s act of taking Bathsheba.’… ‘The oracle accuses David of doing what the rich man in Nathan’s parable does: he takes when he should not.’”

### C-R4-20
**Claim:** **Sword shall never turn aside from your house (priority):** Because David despised the Lord and took Uriah’s wife—family ravaged by sword: Amnon (13:29), Absalom (18:15), Adonijah (1 K 2:25). David’s 11:25 “sword devours one as well as another” returns on him. 1 Sam 2:30 principle still valid (honor/despise). V. 11: raise evil from your house; take wives give to friend (rēʿeykā sg. etymological yod) before your eyes; lie with wives before this sun—refers to Absalom 16:21-22. Secret deed vs public judgment before all Israel and the sun. **Covenant-house inversion:** both ch. 7 and here, “house of David” principal theme—ch. 7 enduring rule promise; here trouble from David’s house. Master’s women “into your bosom”—marrying previous king’s wives may signal throne claim (16:21-22; 1 K 2:17-25) but whether David married Saul’s wives uncertain.
**Quote:** “Now, a sword shall never turn aside from your house… while [ch. 7] gives ‘a promise of continuing rule for David’s house,’ this passage promises ‘trouble to arise from David’s house.’”
**Locus:** slice ll. 596–656; 12:10-12
**Targets:** [[david]], [[nathan]], [[davidic-covenant]], [[david-tsumura]], [[2-samuel]], [[bathsheba]]

### C-R4-21
**Claim:** **12:13 repentance (priority):** David: “I have sinned against the LORD” (ḥāṭāʾtî leYHWH)—unlike Saul’s bare “I have sinned” (1 Sam 15:24). Performative perfect: “I stand convinced of my sin against the Lord”; confession incomplete until sin owned as against Lord and commandments (Ps 51:4). Nathan: “The LORD also has taken away your sin; you shall not die”—performative absolution (Muraoka); lit. cause sin to pass over; McCarter “transferred”; REB “laid on another.” David the anointed does not die (Lev 20:10)—sin transferred to another, his son; yet consequences remain: child shall surely die. **“Insulted [the enemies of] the LORD”:** MT “enemies” likely euphemistic addition (cf. 1 Sam 25:22); 4QSama “word of the LORD” later adjustment; not causative Pi. “caused enemies to blaspheme.” Death of child + three more sons = fourfold penalty David decreed (v. 6). Nathan returns home.
**Quote:** “Unlike Saul who in 1 Sam. 15:24 said simply I have sinned! David confesses his sin against the LORD… The LORD also has taken away your sin; you shall not die… the child who is born to you shall surely die.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 658–690; 12:13-15a
**Targets:** [[david]], [[nathan]], [[bathsheba]], [[davidic-covenant]], [[david-tsumura]], [[2-samuel]]

### C-R4-22
**Claim:** **Ps 51 excursus (priority):** Title: “when Nathan the prophet went to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba”—no reason to dismiss as unhistorical given ANE pre-Davidic hymns with detailed subscriptions. Structure: vv. 1-17 personal sin/forgiveness (heavy 1cs forms); vv. 18-19 recovery of Zion/worship. Literary unity (A…Z / A′Z′): “Have mercy” // “Do good to Zion”; sacrifice/burnt offering rejected // right sacrifices restored. King’s sin affects whole society. “Build walls of Jerusalem” not automatically postexilic (Solomon, Hezekiah repairs); walls = metonymy for Zion recovery as worship place, asked of God not rebuilt by royal fiat alone.
**Quote:** “Psalm 51 was composed on this occasion… A king’s sin does not stop on the personal level; it affects the entire society and kingdom spiritually.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 693–737; EXCURSUS after 12:15a
**Targets:** [[david]], [[nathan]], [[bathsheba]], [[david-tsumura]], [[2-samuel]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R4-23
**Claim:** **Child dies (12:15b-23):** LORD strikes the child (still called “Uriah’s wife’s” child—stress crime / conception status); sick. David seeks God, fasts, goes in, spends night lying on ground (procedural HOW discourse; hendiadys last verbs)—not cult-of-the-dead vestige (son still alive; non-Israelite practice read in). Elders cannot raise him / make him eat. Seventh day child dies; servants fear telling (he may “do evil” = suicide). David perceives whispering, confirms death. Then arises, washes, anoints, changes clothes, enters house of the LORD and worships, eats—stage-spotlight ten wayqtls (Muraoka). bêt YHWH not anachronistic Solomon temple: tent shrine for ark (Ugaritic bt El; Akk bītu “tent”). Purpose baʿăbûr hayyeled ḥay vs situation beʿôd (v. 22) distinguished. “Who knows? The LORD may be gracious”—like prophetic ʾûlay; hoped God change mind. After death: entrusts dead to sovereign merciful God—opposite Canaanite cult of dead; “realistic monotheist.” “I will go to him; he will not come back” = death reunion (Gen 37:35 style), not underworld descent ritual (against Lewis).
**Quote:** “I will go to him, he will not come back to me… David’s behavior has nothing to do with a Canaanite cult of the dead… we may catch a glimpse of the fact that David was a realistic monotheist.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 739–849; 12:15b-23
**Targets:** [[david]], [[bathsheba]], [[nathan]], [[david-tsumura]], [[2-samuel]]

### C-R4-24
**Claim:** **Solomon / Jedidiah (priority) — covenant-despite-sin:** David comforts wife Bathsheba; he comes and lies with her (contrast 11:4 she came / forced-consent frame—still David’s initiative, now comfort). She bears Solomon; **“Now the LORD loved him”**; Nathan sent; names him **Jedidiah** (“Beloved of the LORD”; cf. Ug. ydd il) **for the sake of the LORD** (baʿăbûr YHWH—not over-translate “grace”). Birth can be sign of divine forgiveness after punishment (death of illegitimate child). Q. Bathsheba named / K. “he named.” Solomon etymologies: Mettinger “substitute/replacement” for dead child; “his peace”; Bergen “His [Yahweh’s] Restoration/Peace”; Šlm divine name link elsewhere. 1 Chr 3:5 fourth son—narrative may skip years to thematic end (dischronologization). Jedidiah only here; throne-name vs private-name debate (McCarter et al. vs Firth nickname)—Tsumura: both official possible; Solomon more popular (287×). Solomon offstage until 1 K 1.
**Quote:** “She bore a son and named him Solomon. Now the LORD loved him and sent Nathan the prophet, and he named him Jedidiah for the sake of the LORD… The birth of Solomon could be taken as a sign of divine forgiveness after the divine punishment.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 815–862; 12:24-25
**Targets:** [[solomon]], [[david]], [[bathsheba]], [[nathan]], [[davidic-covenant]], [[david-tsumura]], [[2-samuel]]

### C-R4-25
**Claim:** **Joab at Rabbah / frame close (12:26-31):** Returns to siege after Solomon birth; Joab captures royal city / “city of waters” (water-supply section; royal fortress over Jabbok spring); summons David so David’s name, not Joab’s, called on the city. David captures Rabbah; takes crown of their king (or Milcom?—footnote mark) talent of gold (~33 kg) with precious stone on David’s head (waw existential / casus pendens; Amman statues with huge crowns). Captives put to work with saws, iron instruments, axes—brickmaking (K. malkēn / Q. malbēn); economic exploitation of conquered territory standard. David and people return to Jerusalem—closes Ammonite-Aramean war begun ch. 10, AXB complete.
**Quote:** “This section concludes the long account of David’s Ammonite-Aramean war that began in chapter 10 and was interrupted by the account of David’s sin with Bathsheba, thus constituting the AXB pattern.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 864–904; 12:26-31
**Targets:** [[joab]], [[david]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R4-26
**Claim:** Grace and acceptance despite sin (theological synthesis of pericope): only God’s grace makes David realize how sinful he has been and allows him as a sinner to be accepted again; Lord takes away sin so he shall not die; yet temporal judgment (sword in house; child’s death; fourfold loss of sons) stands; Solomon loved by the LORD / Jedidiah names ongoing elective favor on the Davidic line beyond the crime. Eternal-house prophet Nathan is also judgment-and-absolution messenger—covenant relationship continues under discipline.
**Quote:** “Only God’s grace makes David realize how sinful he has been and allows him as a sinner to be accepted again by the holy sovereign Lord.”
**Locus:** slice ll. 176–177, 664–667, 815–817, 854; intro + 12:13 + 12:24-25
